Traupman 169, 400

pollīnctor, pollīnctōris m.

noun, third declension

one who prepares the dead for burial

Other words

  • libitīnārius, libitīnāriī m. — an undertaker, who provides and runs funerals

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ben. 6.38: dēsignātōrēs et libitīnāriī (Lewis & Short)

    Post-Augustan (Lewis & Short): Seneca names dēsignātōrēs et libitīnāriī, the masters of ceremonies and the undertakers, together. From Libitina, the goddess of funerals.

See also funeral, coffin.
